questions.q: A 25-year-old man presents with painless genital ulcer with indurated edges and clean base. Inguinal lymph nodes are non-tender and firm. Dark-field microscopy shows corkscrew-motility organisms. Which treatment is most appropriate?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum. First-line treatment is benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose. Doxycycline is an alternative for penicillin-allergic patients.

questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic patches and thickened peripheral nerves. Slit skin smear is negative. Skin biopsy shows granulomas with lymphocyte cuffing around nerves with no bacilli. What type of leprosy does he have?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) shows well-formed granulomas with lymphocytes, Langerhans giant cells, nerve damage, and negative slit skin smear (paucibacillary). The skin biopsy finding of granulomas surrounding nerves with lymphocytes and absent bacilli is classic for TT.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with tense bullae over the skin without mucosal involvement. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane zone. Which disorder does she most likely have?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense bullae in elderly patients, spares mucosa, and DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ. Target antigen is BP180 (type XVII collagen) and BP230. Pemphigus shows intraepidermal blister with IgG around keratinocytes.

questions.q: A 20-year-old develops itchy vesicles over the elbows, knees, and buttocks. Skin biopsy shows subepidermal blister with neutrophilic microabscesses at papillary tips. DIF shows granular IgA deposits in dermal papillae. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (Duhring's disease) is associated with gluten-sensitive enteropathy. DIF shows granular IgA deposits in dermal papillae. Neutrophilic microabscesses at papillary tips are characteristic. Linear IgA disease shows linear IgA deposits.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman on long-term chloroquine for lupus presents with bilateral yellow-brown pigmentation of her nails, skin, and hair. Which drug side effect is this?
questions.exp: Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine can cause yellow-brown to grey-blue pigmentation of skin, nails, and hair. It can also cause bull's-eye maculopathy. Regular ophthalmologic monitoring is essential.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive man presents with painless, violaceous, non-pruritic plaques on the skin, oral mucosa, and feet. Biopsy shows spindle cells, extravasated red blood cells, and slit-like vascular spaces. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma in HIV patients is caused by HHV-8. It presents with violaceous plaques/nodules on skin, mucosa, and viscera. Biopsy shows spindle cells, slit-like vascular spaces, and extravasated RBCs. Treatment involves HAART and chemotherapy.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with a pearly translucent papule with telangiectasias on her nose, with a central ulceration. She has a history of significant sun exposure. Which condition is most likely?
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common skin cancer. Nodulo-ulcerative type presents as pearly papule with telangiectasias and 'rodent ulcer'. It arises from basal cells of epidermis, commonly on sun-exposed areas. Treatment: excision, Mohs surgery.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman on oral contraceptives develops brownish symmetrical macules over the cheeks, forehead, and upper lip that worsen in summer. Wood's lamp examination reveals enhanced contrast of the lesions. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Melasma is symmetrical facial hyperpigmentation triggered by UV exposure, pregnancy, or OCP use. Wood's lamp enhances epidermal (superficial) melasma but not dermal type. Treatment: sunscreens, hydroquinone, azelaic acid, chemical peels.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man with a history of psoriasis on methotrexate develops oral ulcers, pancytopenia, and nausea. Which mechanism best explains this toxicity?
questions.exp: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, depleting folate stores needed for DNA synthesis. Toxicity includes mucositis, pancytopenia, hepatotoxicity, and pulmonary fibrosis. Folinic acid (leucovorin) supplementation prevents toxicity without reducing efficacy.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with malar rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, and polyarthritis. ANA is positive (1:640). Anti-dsDNA antibodies are strongly positive. Which finding is most specific for this diagnosis?
questions.exp: Anti-Sm (anti-Smith) antibodies are highly specific for SLE (specificity >99%), though sensitivity is low (~25-30%). Anti-dsDNA is sensitive and correlates with disease activity and nephritis. ANA is sensitive but not specific.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman with progressive skin tightening, Raynaud's phenomenon, and difficulty swallowing has CREST features. Which antibody is most likely positive?
questions.exp: CREST syndrome (Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasias) is associated with anti-centromere antibodies in limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis. Anti-Scl-70 is associated with diffuse systemic sclerosis.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the mouth and nose. Gram stain of exudate shows gram-positive cocci in clusters. What is the first-line treatment?
questions.exp: Impetigo is a superficial bacterial infection caused by Staphylococcus aureus (or Streptococcus pyogenes). For localized cases, topical mupirocin or retapamulin is first-line. Systemic antibiotics are indicated for extensive disease or recurrence.

questions.q: A 35-year-old cattle farmer develops a painless black eschar on the forearm with marked surrounding edema but minimal tenderness. He has mild fever and regional lymphadenopathy. What is the most likely causative organism?
questions.exp: Cutaneous anthrax is caused by Bacillus anthracis. The pathognomonic finding is a painless black eschar (malignant pustule) with marked edema but minimal pain, following contact with infected animals or animal products. Treatment: ciprofloxacin or doxycycline.

questions.q: A 22-year-old sexually active man develops painful inguinal lymphadenopathy (bubo) with groove sign (inguinal ligament dividing the mass). He had a painless genital papule that healed 3 weeks ago. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1-L3. Classic presentation is painless transient genital ulcer followed by painful inguinal bubo. Groove sign (bubo above and below inguinal ligament) is pathognomonic. Treatment: doxycycline 100 mg BD for 21 days.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic patient presents with rapidly spreading cellulitis of the lower limb with crepitus on palpation, bullae, and systemic toxicity. X-ray shows subcutaneous gas. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: Emergency surgical debridement plus IV antibiotics
questions.exp: Necrotizing fasciitis/gas gangrene is a surgical emergency. Subcutaneous gas on X-ray indicates gas-producing organisms (Clostridium or polymicrobial). Treatment requires immediate extensive surgical debridement plus broad-spectrum IV antibiotics. Delay increases mortality significantly.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman develops itchy, ring-shaped scaly lesions on her thigh that expand centrifugally. KOH preparation shows septate hyphae. Which antifungal is the best topical choice?
questions.exp: Tinea corporis (dermatophytosis) is treated with topical azoles (clotrimazole, miconazole) for localized disease. Nystatin is effective only against Candida, not dermatophytes. Systemic griseofulvin or terbinafine is used for extensive or refractory cases.

questions.q: A 30-year-old immunocompromised patient develops fever, disseminated skin lesions appearing as umbilicated papules, and meningitis. India ink preparation of CSF shows encapsulated yeast. What is the treatment of choice?
questions.exp: Cryptococcal meningitis is caused by Cryptococcus neoformans. Umbilicated papules mimicking molluscum contagiosum can occur in disseminated disease. Treatment of choice for CNS disease: induction with Amphotericin B + flucytosine, followed by maintenance with fluconazole.

questions.q: A 20-year-old develops grouped vesicles on an erythematous base along the T5 dermatome. The patient reports burning pain preceding the eruption. Which complication is most feared in elderly patients?
questions.exp: Herpes zoster (shingles) is caused by VZV reactivation. Post-herpetic neuralgia (PHN) is the most common complication, especially in elderly patients (>50 years). It presents as persistent pain lasting months to years after rash resolution. Early antiviral treatment reduces PHN risk.

questions.q: A 5-year-old child develops widespread vesicles on erythematous base in crops, in various stages (macules, papules, vesicles, crusts simultaneously). Parents report he had fever 2 days ago. Which statement about this condition is correct?
opts: Lesions are contagious until all crusts fall off
Patient is non-contagious once vesicles appear
questions.exp: Chickenpox (varicella) caused by VZV. The centripetal rash (starting on trunk) with lesions in various stages is characteristic. Patients are contagious from 2 days before rash to when all lesions crust over. Crusted lesions are still contagious until completely healed.

questions.q: A 24-year-old patient presents with oval salmon-pink macule on the trunk ('herald patch') followed 2 weeks later by multiple similar but smaller lesions in a 'Christmas tree' pattern on the back. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Pityriasis rosea classically begins with a herald patch followed by daughter lesions in a Christmas tree distribution along Langer's lines. It is self-limiting (6-8 weeks). Differential includes secondary syphilis (perform RPR if sexually active).

questions.q: A 35-year-old patient with psoriasis develops joint pain and morning stiffness in the DIP joints of the hands. Nails show pitting, onycholysis, and subungual hyperkeratosis. What type of psoriatic arthritis does he have?
questions.exp: DIP predominant arthritis involves distal interphalangeal joints and is strongly associated with nail psoriasis (pitting, onycholysis). It's the classic pattern seen in psoriatic arthritis. Arthritis mutilans is the most severe destructive form with 'telescoping fingers'.

questions.q: A 16-year-old girl develops comedones, inflammatory papules, and pustules on her face, chest, and back. She is started on isotretinoin. Which monitoring is mandatory?
opts: Lipid profile, liver function, and pregnancy test
questions.exp: Isotretinoin monitoring requires: lipid profile (hypertriglyceridemia risk), LFTs (hepatotoxicity), and mandatory pregnancy testing (highly teratogenic — FDA iPLEDGE program). Two forms of contraception required. CBC monitoring is not mandatory.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman develops itchy, lichenified plaques in the antecubital and popliteal fossa. She has a history of childhood asthma and allergic rhinitis. Serum IgE is markedly elevated. Which finding on skin biopsy is most characteristic?
questions.exp: Atopic dermatitis (eczema) shows spongiosis (intercellular edema), acanthosis, and eosinophilic infiltrate in the dermis. It is part of the atopic triad (eczema, asthma, allergic rhinitis). Associated with elevated IgE and Th2-mediated immune response.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with violaceous planar papules over the wrists and ankles with Wickham's striae. Oral mucosa shows lacy white network. Which treatment is used for recalcitrant cases?
questions.exp: Lichen planus is characterized by 5 P's: purple, pruritic, polygonal, planar papules. Topical corticosteroids are first-line. For widespread or recalcitrant disease, cyclosporine, methotrexate, or systemic steroids are used. Acitretin is preferred for hypertrophic LP.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with multiple pearly papules around the eyes (milia-like), red-brown nodules over the face and neck, and orange-peel skin appearance. Ophthalmoscopy shows angioid streaks. What genetic condition does he have?
questions.exp: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum (PXE) is caused by ABCC6 mutations. Features include yellowish papules on flexures (plucked chicken skin), angioid streaks (ophthalmoscopy), and cardiovascular complications. It affects elastic tissue due to calcification and fragmentation.

questions.q: A 20-year-old patient undergoes a Tzanck smear from the base of a fresh vesicle. The smear shows multinucleated giant cells with nuclear molding. This finding is consistent with which infections?
questions.exp: Tzanck smear showing multinucleated giant cells (Tzanck cells) with nuclear molding is positive in both HSV (herpes simplex) and VZV (varicella-zoster). It cannot differentiate between them. PCR is needed for specific identification. Positive in pemphigus shows acantholytic cells.

questions.q: During a Mohs micrographic surgery for a basal cell carcinoma on the nose, the surgeon maps and processes each tissue layer. What is the main advantage of this technique over standard excision?
opts: Complete margin assessment with tissue sparing
Lower recurrence rate but more scarring
questions.exp: Mohs micrographic surgery allows 100% margin assessment (en face horizontal frozen sections) compared to <1% with conventional bread-loaf sections. This enables maximal tissue preservation while ensuring complete tumor removal. Highest cure rates (99%) for primary BCC.

questions.q: A 45-year-old patient with vitiligo is treated with narrowband UVB phototherapy. The minimum erythema dose (MED) is determined before starting. What is the primary mechanism of action of NBUVB in vitiligo?
opts: Immunosuppression and stimulation of melanocyte migration from hair follicles
questions.exp: NBUVB (311 nm) works in vitiligo through: immunosuppression (reducing T-cell activity against melanocytes) and stimulating melanocyte migration/proliferation from hair follicle reservoirs. Repigmentation typically starts perifolliularly. It's first-line for widespread vitiligo.

questions.q: A 30-year-old male on dapsone for leprosy develops acute hemolytic anemia with Heinz body inclusions on peripheral smear. Which enzyme deficiency predisposes to this complication?
questions.exp: G6PD (glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase) deficiency predisposes to hemolytic anemia when exposed to oxidant drugs like dapsone, primaquine, and sulfonamides. Dapsone causes both hemolysis and methemoglobinemia. G6PD screening before dapsone initiation is recommended.

questions.q: A 35-year-old patient with lepromatous leprosy on rifampicin, clofazimine, and dapsone (MDT) develops acute tender erythematous nodules over the arms and legs with fever, arthralgia, and iridocyclitis. What is this reaction and its treatment?
opts: Type 1 reaction (reversal reaction) — treat with corticosteroids
Type 2 reaction (ENL) — treat with thalidomide or corticosteroids
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL) is a Type 2 lepra reaction occurring in lepromatous leprosy (LL/BL). It is immune complex-mediated (Type III hypersensitivity). Treatment: thalidomide is drug of choice (contraindicated in pregnancy), corticosteroids are alternative. Continue MDT during reactions.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman with long-standing psoriasis develops erythroderma after abrupt withdrawal of systemic corticosteroids. She is febrile and has widespread erythema. What is the greatest immediate risk?
opts: High output cardiac failure and hypothermia
questions.exp: Erythroderma (exfoliative dermatitis) causes loss of normal skin barrier function. Major risks include: high-output cardiac failure (due to increased cutaneous blood flow), hypothermia (heat loss through erythematous skin), electrolyte imbalance, and hypoalbuminemia. Immediate hospitalization is required.
